engine.title: The AI reads the language. The rules engine decides.

steps.title: Read
steps.body: A language model reads English, French and Kreol and marks what the message is doing: urgency, a code request, a payment. Every claim must quote the message.

steps.title: Verify
steps.body: Deterministic checks compare links, senders and payment details with the real addresses of Mauritian banks, telecoms and agencies.

steps.title: Decide
steps.body: A rules engine weighs the evidence and sets the verdict and the advice. The model never does.

engine.note: If the AI is offline, steps 02 and 03 still run and you still get a verdict.

extensionPage.title: FraudLens Link Guard
extensionPage.lede: The extension checks the site you are on against the real addresses of Mauritius banks and telecoms, and can scan a page or a selected message on request. It is not in any browser store yet, so you install it from the project's source.
extensionPage.chromeNote: Works in Chrome 102 or later and in Microsoft Edge.
steps: Download the FraudLens source code as a zip and unzip it.
Click Load unpacked and choose the extension folder inside the unzipped project.
extensionPage.firefoxBody: Not supported yet. The extension is built for Chromium browsers (Manifest V3 service worker), and it has not been packaged or tested for Firefox.
what: Checks each site's address against the real domains of Mauritius banks and telecoms, and marks the toolbar icon.
Scan This Page: reads the page's visible text, never form fields or anything you typed, and checks it.
Right-click a link or selected text to check it.
Security Report: a passive check of a site's HTTPS, headers and cookies.
extensionPage.edgeBody: Same steps as Chrome, on edge://extensions.
extensionPage.outlookNote: Checks the email you have open in Outlook on the web or desktop. Not in the Microsoft store yet, so you add it from a manifest file.
outlookSteps: Go to aka.ms/olksideload. This opens Outlook on the web.
Open My add-ins, then Custom Addins, then Add a custom add-in, then Add from file.
Pick manifest.xml. FraudLens then appears when you open an email.
extensionPage.outlookNoteWork: School and work Microsoft 365 accounts often block custom add-ins. If Custom Addins is missing, ask your IT admin to allow it.

privacyPage.title: Privacy
privacyPage.lede: What FraudLens does with the messages you check, in plain words.

sections.title: Messages you paste
sections.body: Phone numbers, emails and account numbers are removed in your browser before a message is sent for analysis. Links, domains and codes are kept, because the checks depend on them.

sections.title: Screenshots and documents
sections.body: Screenshots and documents are sent to our server as they are. The server reads the text and removes phone numbers, emails and account numbers before anything is analysed.

sections.title: What the server keeps
sections.body: Text sent for analysis is used to produce your result and is not written to a database. When a message is flagged, FraudLens counts its scam type, the institution it claims to be, the sender it shows and any fake links, so Scam trends can show what is circulating. You can turn this off in Settings. Community reports are stored as a one-way fingerprint of the redacted text, never the text itself, and are deleted after 90 days.

sections.title: What stays on your device
sections.body: Your recent checks, your Learn streak and your settings are saved in this browser only. Clearing the site's data removes them.

sections.title: Who else sees it
sections.body: Analysis runs on a language model we host. A hosted provider (currently Anthropic) is used only as a fallback when ours is unavailable. We don't sell data, run ads or use analytics trackers.
